previousNote: The figures at 8cb28f4 that this record replaces. They were built by a generator in which PRESCRIBED RUNNING DAYS ALWAYS EQUALLED AVAILABILITY: the athlete's chosen day count was the divisor the week's volume was spread across, so a 10km week on six available days came out as six one-and-a-half-kilometre runs, and a week that could not fill its days at EASY_MIN_KM was built bigger than it was asked for rather than written across fewer days.
correctionNote:
WHAT MOVED, AND WHY, MEASURED WEEK BY WEEK ACROSS THE SAME 30,080 WEEKS.
Running days are now min(availability, expressibility, max(2, demonstrated sustainable frequency)); the aerobic-dominance ceiling is read against the days the week actually runs on rather than against availability; a back-to-back long run is gated on the same cap; and a day the week does not run on now actually rests in every block, not only in foundation.

THE RACE POPULATION IS BYTE-IDENTICAL. Every count under tallyRace is unchanged, because a race block starts at or above minViableStartKm — where expressibility never binds — and the matrix builds every case from default state, where there is no demonstrated frequency to read. D reaches an athlete only once they have logged three weeks. Foundation blocks are bit-identical too, verified session-by-session across all 512.

EVERY CHANGE IS THEREFORE IN THE ON-RAMP POPULATION, and every recorded class falls except one: week_overshoots_target_declared 3,955 -> 1,276; long_run_shorter_than_easy_run 5,471 -> 3,201; long_run_implausible_for_distance 4,162 -> 3,352; week_one_exceeds_stated_volume 404 -> 150; long_run_shorter_than_quality 992 -> 659; quality_dominates_week 256 -> 167. Mean delivered/target across every week 1.725 -> 1.436; weeks over-prescribed by more than 35% 6,137 -> 3,458; total kilometres prescribed across the matrix 939,834 -> 912,544 against targets totalling 937,935.

THE ONE RISE IS week_over_week_growth_over_10pct, 466 -> 495, and it is a denominator effect that was decomposed before it was accepted. At week level: 795 newly flagged steps, 209 no longer flagged. Of the 795, 490 are weeks whose own TARGET grows more than 10% (the foundation/on-ramp ramp rate, already a separate open question and untouched here), 128 are the expressibility ladder admitting another running day as volume rises, and 177 are the 0.5km presentation quantum on weeks under 10km. 758 of the 795 are at least as close to their own target as they were before. No week grew because more training was prescribed.

quality_dominates_week decomposes the same way: of the 79 newly flagged weeks, the quality kilometres are unchanged in 79 of 79 and the delivered week is smaller in 79 of 79. The fraction rose because the week stopped being padded, not because the session grew.

Continuity: 0 reversals, 0 jumps, 0 unattributed structural steps across 14,280 adjacent pairs. The new attribution 'expressibleRunningDays admits another day' accounts for the steps the ladder introduces.
correctionNoteStage1to4:
STAGE 1-4 MARATHON RE-CUT, DECOMPOSED BEFORE IT WAS ACCEPTED, AND ONLY TWO ENTRIES MOVE.

long_run_shorter_than_quality 659 -> 562. A marathon week may no longer prescribe a quality session longer than its own long run: the legality test was against weekFitCeil (volume x LONG_FRACTION) and the week's ACTUAL long run sits below that wherever a floor, a cutback or the rounding has moved it, so a 12km/week athlete was given a 5km long run and a 7km tempo. The existing defer/substitute ladder now takes that week to an easy run with strides. Marathon-only; 5k, 10k, half and ultra are unchanged at 141, 138, 123 and 154. Six cases remain, all at or below 15km/week, where a 2km fitness checkpoint's warm-up and cool-down make its DAY longer than a 4km long run -- a readiness question about who should receive a marathon block at all, not a geometry one.

week_over_week_growth_over_10pct 495 -> 515, and it is cutback PLACEMENT, decomposed week by week. 63 steps newly flagged, 43 no longer flagged, net +20. The cause is the fifteen-week marathon architecture: with one taper week rather than two the block carries a thirteenth developing week, and the cutback that used to fall outside Peak now falls between the two peak long-run exposures -- which is the approved Peak 1 / absorption / Peak 2 structure, arrived at as a consequence rather than imposed. Moving a cutback moves which steps are exempt from this check, because a rebound after a cutback is correctly not counted as growth.

NOTHING GREW BECAUSE MORE TRAINING WAS PRESCRIBED, and the distribution says so: max growth 1.33, mean 1.152, median 1.14 -- against 1.33, 1.150 and 1.14 before. Measured transitions are identical at 5,076 and total cutback weeks are identical at 880. Of the 63 newly flagged steps, 53 are at or below 13km/week stated volume, 38 are a step of exactly one kilometre (3->4 is 33%, 4->5 is 25%, 5->6 is 20%) and 60 are a step of 2.5km or less. Only 5 are at 20km/week or above, the largest of them 1.12. At these volumes a single presentation quantum exceeds ten per cent of the week, which is a property of the ruler rather than of the training.

descriptive.note: SERIES: 466 -> 495 -> 515 -> 918 -> 819 -> 1114. The last step is the HALF MARATHON moving to bottom-up construction. A linear ramp almost never crosses ten per cent because it is a straight line drawn between two numbers; a week built from sessions does, because real sessions step. The rise is entirely in the half slice -- 5K, 10K, Marathon and Ultra generated output is byte-identical across this change -- and it is the same signature the marathon produced when it made the same move. It is why the measure was demoted to descriptive.

correctionNoteLoadInstrument:
THE WEEKLY-GROWTH MEASURE IS NOW DESCRIPTIVE, AND WHAT REPLACED IT AS THE AUTHORITY IS test/audit/loadProgression.js.

week_over_week_growth_over_10pct IS NOT RE-CUT AS A THRESHOLD. Its number moved from 515 to 918 and that number is recorded under `descriptive` rather than asserted, because HQ has retired the measure as a binary authority rather than relaxed it. Its semantics, its rounding and its cutback exemption are untouched, so the historical series stays comparable: 466 -> 495 -> 515 -> 918. The rise is what made the case against it. The correction that removed the last hidden accounting defect -- a one-slot week being priced at a structure chain it does not receive -- halved the largest absolute jump in the valid marathon population from 13.9km to 7.6km and emptied the >10km class entirely, and this count went UP, because weeks that no longer absorb a phantom quality surplus into their easy runs are honest weeks and honest weeks are noisier. A measure that worsens when the training improves is not measuring the training.

EIGHT SUSPECT CODES REPLACE IT, one per named reason, so no family hides inside another's total: load_progression_structure_introduced_with_dose_step 723, load_progression_rebound_exceeds_trend 630, load_progression_quality_structure_step 383, load_progression_long_run_step_above_rate 291, load_progression_compound_load_progression 167, load_progression_exceeds_two_week_backstop 76, load_progression_broad_load_increase 49, and load_progression_taper_load_increase at zero everywhere. These are FIRST CUTS of a new measure and are not comparable to the old one: they answer a different question. Each is ratcheted from here.

correctionNoteStructuralHold:
THE STRUCTURAL-TRANSITION HOLD. Marathon prescription changes, so the audit counts change with it, and every one of them moves DOWN except two that are explained below.

WHAT WAS WRONG. "The week a purpose arrives is a week the doses hold" existed in the runtime and had never fired: it compared mWeek.qSlots and mWeek.supportDays -- the BLOCK's constants, the same every week -- against mPrevQSlots and mPrevSupportDays, which were assigned from those same constants two lines later. Neither comparison could ever be true. The week's real structure is decided afterwards, by the capacity gate. The weekly-load instrument at 5d8716d is what found it.

WHAT REPLACED IT. The week is solved TWICE. Once at the doses this step of the progression offers; and where that week would give the athlete a structure they have never been prescribed -- another running day, a first or second quality session, or marathon-specific work entering the long run -- again around the same structure at the workload they have already earned. The second answer is what they receive. The block carries the number of steps ACTUALLY TAKEN rather than a week counter, so a held week costs one step; the rate is fixed at the block's solve and never re-derived, so no later week can be walked faster to make it up. There is no debt and no catch-up: measured across the valid population, the progression index never advances more than one step in a week.

MEASURED: 395 structural arrivals, 383 held at the earned workload, 12 not held because holding would have refused the very session that arrived, 0 retriggers of an established structure. 351 of the 383 held the long run exactly; the rest are Peak weeks, where the peak exposure is chosen by the phase and not by the progression. 367 arrivals still moved the week's total up, median +2.2km -- that is session geometry, chiefly a second or third supporting run that cannot be written below EASY_MIN_KM.

AND A CUTBACK IS A REDUCTION. The taper already had a ladder for a week that comes out larger than the one before it; a cutback needs the same one, because its doses come from the ordinary progression while the week before it may have been suppressed by a hold. Cutback weeks larger than their predecessor: 47 before the hold existed, 77 with it, 10 with the ladder -- all at 6-8km/week where the supporting runs are already at the floor.

THE LOAD-PROGRESSION FAMILIES, marathon, production-valid domain, 5d8716d -> here: compound_load_progression 162 -> 75; exceeds_two_week_backstop 58 -> 18; broad_load_increase 48 -> 24; quality_structure_step 240 -> 164; long_run_step_above_rate 137 -> 103; structure_introduced_with_dose_step 304 -> 291; and the descriptive percentage 441 -> 342. rebound_exceeds_trend rises 125 -> 162 and is arithmetic rather than load: a rebound is measured against the week before the cutback, and that week is now sometimes a held one, so the ratio to it is larger while the sessions still step at the same fixed rate.

structure_introduced_with_dose_step barely moves because the audit is right to keep reporting it. Its 291 survivors decompose into 61 checkpoint weeks (a pinned measurement whose day is a time trial plus its flanks, not a new structure), 57 first-quality weeks whose session is simply larger than the supporting run it replaced, 46 running-day arrivals where EASY_MIN_KM forces the week up, and 16 medium-long arrivals, which the DAY builder decides and the week-level hold therefore cannot reach. Median +1 to +3.6km each.

EVERY VALID-DOMAIN INVARIANT IS UNCHANGED AT ZERO: long_run_shorter_than_quality, long_run_shorter_than_easy_run, volume_unattributed, long_run_zero_distance, zero_km_work_segment, generator_invariant_failure, quality_dominates_week, week_one_exceeds_stated_volume, week_overshoots_target_declared, taper_week_increases_volume.
